data.one_liner: Request display refresh rates and measure Flutter frame cadence, benchmarks, and performance telemetry.
data.what_it_does: Allows requesting high refresh rates on Android and provides multi-platform diagnostics, live overlays, and benchmark reporting. It captures frame cadences, phase overruns, and session statistics.
use_when: You need to request higher refresh rates (e.g. 120 Hz) on Android devices for smoother animations or games.
You want to measure frame cadence, UI/raster budget overruns, and export performance benchmark reports.
avoid_when: You are relying on it to directly control refresh rates on iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, or Web where engine control is unsupported.
You are looking for general state management or standard widget libraries.
strengths: Supports fine-grained preference management via leases, declarative scopes, and automatic policies.
Provides comprehensive session benchmarks, threshold evaluations, and diagnostic exports.
weaknesses: Native refresh rate control is platform-dependent and primarily effective on Android.
Physical presentation FPS cannot be directly measured on certain platforms.
data.setup_notes: For iOS ProMotion devices, you may add the CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone boolean to your Info.plist dictionary.
